objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus adhesive in reducing motion artifacts and improving signal quality in low perfusion conditions using the polymer film attached to the pulse oximeter sensor.
controls: Current pulse oximeter sensor with no polymer film attachment
Standard pulse oximeter sensor with no polymer film attachment
baseline: Current pulse oximeter sensor with no polymer film attachment
procedure: Prepare the pulse oximeter sensor with the Nucleus adhesive and attach the polymer film.
Expose the sensor to low perfusion conditions (SpO2 < 80%) with 10% motion artifact.
Measure the MAR Index using the sensor with the polymer film attachment.
Repeat steps 1-3 for the standard pulse oximeter sensor with no polymer film attachment.
expected_result: A 25% reduction in MAR Index in low perfusion conditions (SpO2 < 80%) with 10% motion artifact.
falsification_condition: Failure to achieve a 20% reduction in MAR Index in at least 80% of low perfusion conditions (SpO2 < 80%) with 10% motion artifact.
sample_requirements: A minimum of 30 pulse oximeter sensors with the Nucleus adhesive and polymer film attachment, and 30 standard pulse oximeter sensors with no polymer film attachment.
safety_constraints: Ensure proper handling and storage of the pulse oximeter sensors to prevent damage or contamination.
information_gain: Understanding the effectiveness of the Nucleus adhesive in reducing motion artifacts and improving signal quality in low perfusion conditions, and identifying potential areas for improvement in the design and implementation of the polymer film attachment.
